adelaide-37.name: Kingston Park Coastal Reserve
adelaide-37.bio: Clifftop reserve at Kingston Park with Holdfast Bay views, the Tjilbruke Spring and a rock sculpture of its Dreaming story.
adelaide-37.ticket_note: Council-managed open reserve with no single steward site verified (City of Holdfast Bay page returned a bot-wall status 202).

notes.text: Free (SATC listing). Cliff-top lookout over Holdfast Bay, Tjilbruke Spring and the John Dowie rock sculpture, 76 indigenous plant species; picnic area, barbecues, toilets.
notes.pin: Lookout and John Dowie rock sculpture on the clifftop off Strickland Road, Kingston Park (SATC address); Tjilbruke Spring is below the cliff.

adelaide-38.name: Adelaide Dolphin Sanctuary
adelaide-38.bio: Marine park in the Port River and Barker Inlet, home to about 20 resident bottlenose dolphins that visitors see on cruises.

notes.text: Parks page: free entry, about 20 resident bottlenose dolphins plus around 400 transient visitors, 10,000-year-old mangrove forest. Dolphin cruises are separate operators, not priced here.
notes.pin: Pin is a Wikivoyage geotag on the water; keep in the Port River near Port Adelaide (Dolphin Sanctuary is a water body; a visitor point such as the Port Adelaide waterfront or Garden Island boat launch is the alternative).

adelaide-39.name: National Railway Museum
adelaide-39.bio: Australia's largest railway museum, in the former Port Dock goods terminal, with locomotives, carriages and a small train ride.

notes.text: Adult $19, concession $12, child 5-15 $7, family $44 (nrm.org.au Plan your visit). Open daily 10am-4:30pm. Wikivoyage's older prices are out of date. Train ride included in admission.
notes.pin: 76 Lipson Street, Port Adelaide; draft is the Wikivoyage geotag.

adelaide-40.name: South Australian Maritime Museum
adelaide-40.bio: Maritime history museum at Port Adelaide, with a climbable lighthouse and the historic waterfront outside.

notes.text: Adult $23.50, concession $18.50, child $9.50 (museum site). Free guided tours weekends 11am and 2pm. Lighthouse climb and MV Archie Badenoch Port River tours are booked separately.

adelaide-41.name: South Australian Aviation Museum
adelaide-41.bio: Port Adelaide museum in two hangars of historic aircraft, jet fighters and Woomera rockets, with cockpits visitors can climb into.

notes.text: Adult $17 (first listed price on saam.org.au Visit page, followed by $8.50 ADF/veterans, $12 concession, $7.50 child, $41.50 family, then free). Open 10am-4pm daily except Christmas Day.

adelaide-42.name: Port Adelaide Historical Society Museum
adelaide-42.bio: Small volunteer-run museum at Port Adelaide with a maritime collection, ship models and audio-visual displays.
adelaide-42.ticket_note: Operator site not found: guessed domains (phsa.org.au, portadelaidehistoricalsociety.org/.com.au/.org.au) did not load; the SATC page exposes no website link in the fetched text.

notes.text: Admission $5 per SATC listing only; not confirmed on an operator page. Marginal: volunteer-run, one counted source (as the draft note says). Keep, but opening days not verified.
notes.pin: Draft coordinates -34.832468,138.496529 are provisional; confirm against the museum's address on the serial pass.

adelaide-43.name: Fort Glanville Conservation Park
adelaide-43.bio: Fort at Semaphore Park, built in 1880, with guided tours and costumed drills and cannon firing on open Sundays.

notes.text: Parks page: open days with re-enactments third Sunday of the month Sep-May 1-4:30pm, adult $20, child $10, family $40, entry includes guided tour. Tuesday tours 9:30-11am $10 per person, bookings preferred. Price range 10-20 reflects Tuesday vs open-day adult. Draft said 1878; the park page says built in 1880.
notes.pin: Draft coordinates provisional (Wikivoyage); fort entrance off Military Road, Semaphore Park.

adelaide-44.name: Coopers Brewery
adelaide-44.bio: Family-owned brewery at Regency Park with a visitor centre, a free self-guided history walk and guided tours with tastings.

notes.text: Visitor Centre Tour $35pp (Tue-Fri 4pm, 60 min); Brewery Tour $50pp ($55 from 1 July 2026; Tue-Sat 9:30am/10:30am/12:30pm, 90 min); VIP $350pp by appointment. The History Walk is free and self-guided. Tours bookable only.
notes.pin: Coopers Brewery, 461 South Road, Regency Park (provisional draft pin from Wikivoyage).

adelaide-45.name: Carrick Hill
adelaide-45.bio: 1930s house museum set in 100 acres of gardens and bushland at Springfield, in the Adelaide foothills.

notes.text: House Museum entry with audio tour: adult $20, concession $18, children under 15 free (SATC). Gardens and grounds are free. House Museum is closed in July each year; grounds open Wednesday to Sunday, 10am-4:30pm (SATC). Official site title is 'Carrick Hill'. The steward's own admission page could not be loaded, so the price rests on the SATC listing.
notes.pin: 46 Carrick Hill Drive, Springfield (SATC address); use the house or main visitor entrance, not the estate centroid.

adelaide-46.name: Warriparinga
adelaide-46.bio: Kaurna cultural site on the Sturt River in Bedford Park, with a cultural centre, a guided walk and the start of the Tjilbruke Trail.
adelaide-46.ticket_note: Council site (marion.sa.gov.au) blocked to scripts; needs a browser check before a link is added.

notes.text: Cost and hours not verified: marion.sa.gov.au returns an async 202 to scripts. Centre believed free to enter with the guided walk charged; recorded as free pending a browser check. Wikipedia: 3.5 ha reserve, Living Kaurna Cultural Centre, heritage-listed farmhouse, start of the Tjilbruke Trail.
notes.pin: Draft -35.020696,138.562991 provisional; Wikipedia says the reserve is bordered by Marion, Sturt and South Roads; use the cultural centre.

adelaide-47.name: Adelaide Arcade
adelaide-47.bio: Heritage-listed Victorian shopping arcade off Rundle Mall, opened in 1885, with a free self-guided history tour and a museum.

notes.text: Opened December 1885; free self-guided history tour and Adelaide Arcade Museum (arcade site). Free to walk through.

adelaide-48.name: Victoria Square
adelaide-48.bio: Central city square known as Tarntanyangga, with the Three Rivers fountain and a place in Kaurna and Aboriginal flag history.
adelaide-48.ticket_note: Open council square: no single operator site.

notes.text: Free open square (City of Adelaide visitor site per draft). Name Tarntanyangga is its Kaurna name. Bio claims rest on the draft's source note (fountain, Kaurna significance, Aboriginal flag first flown) and were not re-fetched; city visitor page URLs tried returned 404.
notes.pin: Keep the draft square centre; Three Rivers fountain is at the centre of the square.
